clue.text: Mixed saunas in this resort

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of saunas are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday resort known for its unisex saunas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like it describes saunas open to both sexes, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, is a well-known holiday destination.

clue.text: A large number of Romans, on balance, is enough

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
to equate is to set two things in balance

explanation.surface: Many Romans, all things considered, are sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans' are not people but Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient for the purpose.

clue.text: Temporary substitutes block passes

explanation.surface: Makeshift replacements are used to obstruct mountain routes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as two words: to stop, or block, the gaps, or passes through mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift measures that fill in until something better comes; and to plug openings, as gaps are mountain passes.

clue.text: Less than agreed! That's rare

parts.note: under means below or less than
done! is said to seal a deal, so it means agreed

explanation.surface: Getting less than was agreed is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' looks like unusual, but it is meat that is lightly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare steak is lightly cooked, not cooked through.

clue.text: Upset relation from Asia

indicators.note: upset means the letters of relation are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative from the East who is upset about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is an old adjective meaning of the East, especially of Asia.

clue.text: Novel liked by both of us

explanation.surface: A book that two people both enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Dickens's last completed one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens novel of 1865; and a person who is a companion to two people at once.

clue.text: Sort of prince that can make one cross

explanation.surface: A kind of prince who can annoy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the X marked on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A Prince-Elector chose the Holy Roman Emperor; and a voter marks a ballot paper with an X.

clue.text: Terriers' excessive enthusiasm for island

parts.note: the Terriers are members of the TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, so this is TA's
a mania is an excessive enthusiasm or craze

explanation.surface: Terrier dogs are over-keen on getting to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' look like dogs, but it is the old nickname for Territorial Army soldiers, abbreviated TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state south of mainland Australia.

clue.text: The line is drawn where such freedom is zero

definitions.text: The line is drawn where such freedom is zero

parts.words: The line is drawn where such freedom is zero
parts.note: reads as a limit on liberty, but the line is the equator, drawn on maps where this measure is zero degrees

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing the line' suggests setting limits on freedom; the line is literal, on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means scope or freedom, and also angular distance from the equator.

clue.text: Instrument sometimes needed to make judgments

explanation.surface: A device that is occasionally required when reaching decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a Recorder is a part-time judge sitting in the Crown Court, so one is needed to make judgments only some of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind pipe played by schoolchildren; also the title of a part-time judge in English courts.

clue.text: High society

parts.note: a jet flies high, so it can stand for something high up
a set is a social group or circle

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and its two words also build it: the jet that flies high plus the set that is a social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy fashionable people who fly between glamorous places were dubbed this in the jet age.

clue.text: Psychologist joins foreign woman in the Alps

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss psychologist
Frau is German for a woman or wife

explanation.surface: A psychologist meets a woman from abroad on an Alpine holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a famous peak in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland.

clue.text: Sound but difficult position

explanation.surface: Something seems healthy yet is actually a tricky predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as healthy, but here it is a narrow sea channel such as Plymouth Sound; the plural of the second sense gives 'dire straits'.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow channel of water linking two seas; also a tight spot, as in being in dire straits.

clue.text: Mix up record manufacturer

indicators.note: mix means the letters of up record are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A company that makes records muddles up an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix up' reads as a phrase, but 'up' is part of the fodder and 'Mix' alone is the anagram signal; 'record manufacturer' also looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is one who makes goods, a maker.

clue.text: Cite a University don as possible provider of this

definitions.text: Cite a University don as possible provider of this

indicators.note: possible means the letters are one possible rearrangement of the fodder

explanation.surface: Name a university lecturer as someone who might supply schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges CITEAUDON, made from 'Cite a', U and 'don'; the whole clue also defines the answer, since a don provides teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A university lecturer provides teaching and learning to students.

clue.text: Musical heroine was a dark horse

explanation.surface: The leading lady of a show turned out to be an unexpected success.
explanation.walkthrough: Bess is the heroine of Gershwin's Porgy and Bess; Black Bess was the horse of the highwayman Dick Turpin in English legend, so she was literally a dark horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The female lead of Porgy and Bess; and the black mare ridden by Dick Turpin.

clue.text: Level of interest in powers' speed

parts.note: the banks are the financial powers, so this stands for a bank's
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: How keen the authorities are on going fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level of interest' looks like enthusiasm, but it is the interest charged on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: The rate set by a central bank governs the interest charged on borrowing.

clue.text: After a second, falls — or almost does

indicators.note: after means the word for falls comes following the abbreviation for a second

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a second
tumbles means falls

explanation.surface: Someone takes a moment and then falls, or nearly does.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'falls': to trip is to almost fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip and lurch is nearly to fall over.

clue.text: Record first reached by fastest runner

explanation.surface: An athlete sets a new record by getting somewhere ahead of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To record is to capture on magnetic strip; the winner of a race breaks the strip stretched over the finishing line.

clue.text: Booming old headmaster keeps in sixth form

indicators.note: keeps in means the headmaster holds the next piece inside him

parts.note: Edward Thring was the famous Victorian headmaster of Uppingham School

indicators.note: form means the letters VI are formed into a new order

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six, sixth

explanation.surface: A thriving old head teacher detains pupils in the sixth form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges VI into IV, which 'keeps in' places inside THRING; 'sixth form' looks like the top class at a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: A booming business is one doing very well, flourishing.

clue.text: Caps meat paste with litre of ale perhaps

parts.note: pâté is a meat paste

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters of ale are offered in another possible order

explanation.surface: Someone tops a meat paste with a litre of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALE into LAE; 'Caps' looks like a verb but is the plural noun, kneecaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneecaps are the bones at the front of the knees.

clue.text: It causes ringing in the ears when one is depressed

definitions.text: It causes ringing in the ears when one is depressed

parts.words: It causes ringing in the ears when one is depressed
parts.note: sounds like tinnitus brought on by gloom, but 'depressed' means physically pressed down, as a doorbell button is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' suggests low spirits; it means pushed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A button pressed to sound an electric bell, typically at a front door.

clue.text: Powerful feller players spotted

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, players
saw means spotted, noticed

explanation.surface: Musicians noticed a strong man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like a fellow; it is something that fells, here a power-driven cutting blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A power saw with a continuous steel band blade cuts timber.

clue.text: Garment doctor displayed in family circle

indicators.note: in means the doctor is placed inside the word for family

parts.note: kin means family or relatives
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
O is round, so it stands for a circle

explanation.surface: A doctor shows off clothing among the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, wide-sleeved Japanese robe, a traditional item of clothing.

clue.text: Fetched one after genuine final letter

indicators.note: after means the numeral for one follows the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
I is the Roman numeral one
zed is the British name for Z, the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone collected one item after the true last letter arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetched' looks like went and got, but it means sold for, as an item at auction fetches or realizes a price.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sale, goods that fetch a sum make or bring in that amount.

clue.text: A fortunate combination, most talented

parts.note: blest, an old spelling of blessed, means fortunate

explanation.surface: A lucky combination of the most gifted people.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or skilled; the superlative is the most capable.

clue.text: Match-fit?

parts.note: reads as a sportsman ready to play, but a match is a marriage, so this is someone suitable to marry

explanation.definitionFit: An eligible bachelor is one considered a desirable marriage partner.

clue.text: Such a course is contrary to young man's advice

definitions.text: Such a course is contrary to young man's advice

parts.words: Such a course is contrary to young man's advice
parts.note: the advice is the American saying 'Go west, young man', so the course opposite to it heads the other way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west, young man' was a 19th-century American slogan urging settlers towards the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the sunrise, the opposite direction to west.

clue.text: A sort of ginger brown colour

indicators.note: a sort of means the letters of ginger are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A gingery shade of brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a dated colour name, now recognised as a racial slur and no longer used; it appeared in paint and fabric catalogues of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A former trade name for a dark brown shade, now offensive and obsolete.
